audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim warfare, exemptions, siege, and fruit-tree law, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for priestly battle address, fear, house/vineyard/betrothal exemptions, fainthearted release, peace offer and forced labor, total-destruction commands, siege limits, fruit-tree protection, and anti-war safeguards.

verses.restored: When you go out to battle against your enemies and see horse and chariot, a people more numerous than you, you shall not fear them, for YHWH your Divine is with you, who brought you up from land of Egypt.

familiar.text: When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for the LORD thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

modern.text: When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them; for the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, is with you.

original.text: כִּֽי תֵצֵ֨א לַמִּלְחָמָ֜ה עַל אֹיְבֶ֗יךָ וְֽרָאִ֜יתָ ס֤וּס וָרֶ֨כֶב֙ עַ֚ם רַ֣ב מִמְּךָ֔ לֹ֥א תִירָ֖א מֵהֶ֑ם כִּֽי יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ הַמַּֽעַלְךָ֖ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: It shall be, when you draw near to battle, priest shall approach and speak to people.

familiar.text: And it shall be, when ye are come nigh unto the battle, that the priest shall approach and speak unto the people,

modern.text: When you are about to go into battle, the priest is to come forward and address the army,

original.text: וְהָיָ֕ה כְּקָֽרָבְכֶ֖ם אֶל הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְנִגַּ֥שׁ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְדִבֶּ֥ר אֶל הָעָֽם

verses.restored: He shall say to them, Hear, Israel: You draw near today to battle against your enemies. Let not your heart soften; do not fear, panic, or tremble before them.

familiar.text: And shall say unto them, Hear, O Israel, ye approach this day unto battle against your enemies: let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble, neither be ye terrified because of them;

modern.text: saying to them, “Hear, O Israel, today you are going into battle with your enemies. Do not be fainthearted or afraid; do not be alarmed or terrified because of them.

original.text: וְאָמַ֤ר אֲלֵהֶם֙ שְׁמַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתֶּ֨ם קְרֵבִ֥ים הַיּ֛וֹם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עַל אֹיְבֵיכֶ֑ם אַל יֵרַ֣ךְ לְבַבְכֶ֗ם אַל תִּֽירְא֧וּ וְאַֽל תַּחְפְּז֛וּ וְאַל תַּֽעַרְצ֖וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: For YHWH your Divine is the one going with you to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.

familiar.text: For the LORD your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.

modern.text: For the LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies, to give you the victory.”

original.text: כִּ֚י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם הַהֹלֵ֖ךְ עִמָּכֶ֑ם לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם לָכֶ֛ם עִם אֹיְבֵיכֶ֖ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶתְכֶֽם

verses.restored: Officers shall speak to people, saying, Who is the man who built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in battle and another man dedicate it.

familiar.text: And the officers shall speak unto the people, saying, What man is there that hath built a new house, and hath not dedicated it? let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man dedicate it.

modern.text: Furthermore, the officers are to address the army, saying, “Has any man built a new house and not dedicated it? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man dedicate it.

original.text: וְדִבְּר֣וּ הַשֹּֽׁטְרִים֮ אֶל הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ מִֽי הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנָ֤ה בַֽיִת חָדָשׁ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֲנָכ֔וֹ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יַחְנְכֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: Who is the man who planted a vineyard and has not begun to enjoy it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in battle and another man begin to enjoy it.

familiar.text: And what man is he that hath planted a vineyard, and hath not yet eaten of it? let him also go and return unto his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man eat of it.

modern.text: Has any man planted a vineyard and not begun to enjoy its fruit? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man enjoy its fruit.

original.text: וּמִֽי הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁר נָטַ֥ע כֶּ֨רֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א חִלְּל֔וֹ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יְחַלְּלֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: Who is the man who betrothed a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in battle and another man take her.

familiar.text: And what man is there that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her? let him go and return unto his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man take her.

modern.text: Has any man become pledged to a woman and not married her? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man marry her.”

original.text: וּמִֽי הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵרַ֤שׂ אִשָּׁה֙ וְלֹ֣א לְקָחָ֔הּ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יִקָּחֶֽנָּה

verses.restored: Officers shall continue to speak to people and say, Who is the man fearful and soft of heart? Let him go and return to his house, so heart of his brothers does not melt like his heart.

familiar.text: And the officers shall speak further unto the people, and they shall say, What man is there that is fearful and fainthearted? let him go and return unto his house, lest his brethren’s heart faint as well as his heart.

modern.text: Then the officers shall speak further to the army, saying, “Is any man afraid or fainthearted? Let him return home, so that the hearts of his brothers will not melt like his own.”

original.text: וְיָסְפ֣וּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים֮ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל הָעָם֒ וְאָמְר֗וּ מִי הָאִ֤ישׁ הַיָּרֵא֙ וְרַ֣ךְ הַלֵּבָ֔ב יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יִמַּ֛ס אֶת לְבַ֥ב אֶחָ֖יו כִּלְבָבֽוֹ

verses.restored: When officers finish speaking to people, they shall appoint commanders of hosts at head of people.

familiar.text: And it shall be, when the officers have made an end of speaking unto the people, that they shall make captains of the armies to lead the people.

modern.text: When the officers have finished addressing the army, they are to appoint commanders to lead it.

original.text: וְהָיָ֛ה כְּכַלֹּ֥ת הַשֹּׁטְרִ֖ים לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל הָעָ֑ם וּפָֽקְד֛וּ שָׂרֵ֥י צְבָא֖וֹת בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הָעָֽם

verses.restored: When you draw near to a city to fight against it, you shall call to it for peace.

familiar.text: When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it.

modern.text: When you approach a city to fight against it, you are to make an offer of peace.

original.text: כִּֽי תִקְרַ֣ב אֶל עִ֔יר לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עָלֶ֑יהָ וְקָרָ֥אתָ אֵלֶ֖יהָ לְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: It shall be, if it answers you peace and opens to you, then all people found in it shall become forced labor for you and serve you.

familiar.text: And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.

modern.text: If they accept your offer of peace and open their gates, all the people there will become forced laborers to serve you.

original.text: וְהָיָה֙ אִם שָׁל֣וֹם תַּֽעַנְךָ֔ וּפָתְחָ֖ה לָ֑ךְ וְהָיָ֞ה כָּל הָעָ֣ם הַנִּמְצָא בָ֗הּ יִהְי֥וּ לְךָ֛ לָמַ֖ס וַעֲבָדֽוּךָ

verses.restored: But if it does not make peace with you and makes war with you, then you shall besiege it.

familiar.text: And if it will make no peace with thee, but will make war against thee, then thou shalt besiege it:

modern.text: But if they refuse to make peace with you and wage war against you, lay siege to that city.

original.text: וְאִם לֹ֤א תַשְׁלִים֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ וְעָשְׂתָ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְצַרְתָּ֖ עָלֶֽיהָּ

verses.restored: YHWH your Divine will give it into your hand, and you shall strike every male in it with edge of sword.

familiar.text: And when the LORD thy God hath delivered it into thine hands, thou shalt smite every male thereof with the edge of the sword:

modern.text: When the LORD your God has delivered it into your hand, you must put every male to the sword.

original.text: וּנְתָנָ֛הּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְהִכִּיתָ֥ אֶת כָּל זְכוּרָ֖הּ לְפִי חָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Only women, little ones, livestock, and all in city, all its spoil, you may plunder for yourself; you shall eat spoil of your enemies YHWH your Divine gives you.

familiar.text: But the women, and the little ones, and the cattle, and all that is in the city, even all the spoil thereof, shalt thou take unto thyself; and thou shalt eat the spoil of thine enemies, which the LORD thy God hath given thee.

modern.text: But the women, children, livestock, and whatever else is in the city—all its spoil—you may take as plunder, and you shall use the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God gives you.

original.text: רַ֣ק הַ֠נָּשִׁים וְהַטַּ֨ף וְהַבְּהֵמָ֜ה וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה בָעִ֛יר כָּל שְׁלָלָ֖הּ תָּבֹ֣ז לָ֑ךְ וְאָֽכַלְתָּ֙ אֶת שְׁלַ֣ל אֹיְבֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Thus you shall do to all cities very far from you, which are not from cities of these nations here.

familiar.text: Thus shalt thou do unto all the cities which are very far off from thee, which are not of the cities of these nations.

modern.text: This is how you are to treat all the cities that are far away from you and do not belong to the nations nearby.

original.text: כֵּ֤ן תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ לְכָל הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים הָרְחֹקֹ֥ת מִמְּךָ֖ מְאֹ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא מֵעָרֵ֥י הַגּֽוֹיִם הָאֵ֖לֶּה הֵֽנָּה

verses.restored: But from cities of these peoples YHWH your Divine gives you as inheritance, you shall not let any breath live.

familiar.text: But of the cities of these people, which the LORD thy God doth give thee for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth:

modern.text: However, in the cities of the nations that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you must not leave alive anything that breathes.

original.text: רַ֗ק מֵעָרֵ֤י הָֽעַמִּים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָ֑ה לֹ֥א תְחַיֶּ֖ה כָּל נְשָׁמָֽה

verses.restored: You shall surely devote them to destruction: Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite, as YHWH your Divine commanded you,

familiar.text: But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the LORD thy God hath commanded thee:

modern.text: For you must devote them to complete destruction —the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—as the LORD your God has commanded you,

original.text: כִּֽי הַחֲרֵ֣ם תַּחֲרִימֵ֗ם הַחִתִּ֤י וְהָאֱמֹרִי֙ הַכְּנַעֲנִ֣י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: so they do not teach you to do according to all their abominations they did for their gods, and you sin/misalign against YHWH your Divine.

familiar.text: That they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods; so should ye sin against the LORD your God.

modern.text: so that they cannot teach you to do all the detestable things they do for their gods, and so cause you to sin against the LORD your God.

original.text: לְמַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא יְלַמְּד֤וּ אֶתְכֶם֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כְּכֹל֙ תּֽוֹעֲבֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ לֵֽאלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַחֲטָאתֶ֖ם לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: When you besiege a city many days to fight against it and capture it, you shall not destroy its trees by wielding axe against them, for from them you may eat, and you shall not cut them down. For is tree of field a human, to enter before you in siege?

familiar.text: When thou shalt besiege a city a long time, in making war against it to take it, thou shalt not destroy the trees thereof by forcing an axe against them: for thou mayest eat of them, and thou shalt not cut them down (for the tree of the field is man’s life) to employ them in the siege:

modern.text: When you lay siege to a city for an extended time while fighting against it to capture it, you must not destroy its trees by putting an axe to them, because you can eat their fruit. You must not cut them down. Are the trees of the field human, that you should besiege them?

original.text: כִּֽי תָצ֣וּר אֶל עִיר֩ יָמִ֨ים רַבִּ֜ים לְֽהִלָּחֵ֧ם עָלֶ֣יהָ לְתָפְשָׂ֗הּ לֹֽא תַשְׁחִ֤ית אֶת עֵצָהּ֙ לִנְדֹּ֤חַ עָלָיו֙ גַּרְזֶ֔ן כִּ֚י מִמֶּ֣נּוּ תֹאכֵ֔ל וְאֹת֖וֹ לֹ֣א תִכְרֹ֑ת כִּ֤י הָֽאָדָם֙ עֵ֣ץ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לָבֹ֥א מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ בַּמָּצֽוֹר

verses.restored: Only a tree you know is not a tree for food, it you may destroy and cut down, and build siegeworks against city making war with you until it falls.

familiar.text: Only the trees which thou knowest that they be not trees for meat, thou shalt destroy and cut them down; and thou shalt build bulwarks against the city that maketh war with thee, until it be subdued.

modern.text: But you may destroy the trees that you know do not produce fruit. Use them to build siege works against the city that is waging war against you, until it falls.

original.text: רַ֞ק עֵ֣ץ אֲשֶׁר תֵּדַ֗ע כִּֽי לֹא עֵ֤ץ מַאֲכָל֙ ה֔וּא אֹת֥וֹ תַשְׁחִ֖ית וְכָרָ֑תָּ וּבָנִ֣יתָ מָצ֗וֹר עַל הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁר הִ֨וא עֹשָׂ֧ה עִמְּךָ֛ מִלְחָמָ֖ה עַ֥ד רִדְתָּֽהּ

translation_notes: The chapter contains both restraints on warfare and severe permissions for domination and extermination.
House, vineyard, betrothal, and fear exemptions protect unfinished civilian life and allow the fainthearted to leave without punishment.
The peace offer still imposes forced labor and therefore is not peace by modern standards.
Women and children are treated as plunder in distant-city warfare; this must be named as dehumanizing and never normalized.
Verses 16-17 command total destruction of local peoples and are categorically rejected as models for modern conduct.
Fruit trees are protected during siege because they sustain future life; the rhetorical question distinguishes life-giving ecology from military targets.
The fruit-tree principle does not redeem or sanitize the surrounding war system.
safety_note: Never use Deuteronomy 20 to justify holy war, genocide, forced labor, enslavement, captive-taking, sexual violence, plunder, or environmental destruction. Preserve its exemptions and fruit-tree restraint while categorically refusing the chapter's coercive and exterminatory permissions.
